scenes.text: A 100-year-old book about ancient Babylon has one money rule that most people still get wrong.
Mike and Jake both get paid $3,000.
Mike pays rent, bills, a new phone, dinners out... and plans to save whatever is left.
End of the month? Nothing is left. Every single time.
Jake follows the book's first rule: a part of all you earn is yours to keep. Before paying anyone, he moves 10%, $300, to himself.

props.quote: "A part of all you earn is yours to keep."

scenes.text: He lives on the other 90%. Honestly, he barely notices.
Then rule two: make your gold work for you. He invests it, and the earnings start earning too.
Jake has over $21,000 working for him, at about 7% a year.
Mike? Still waiting for something to be left over.
Don't save what's left after spending. Spend what's left after saving.
Follow for more lessons from the richest man in Babylon.

props.disclaimer: Educational story, not financial advice. Returns are not guaranteed.
